history.sg_progress: The Administration will continue to request entities to comply with General Assembly resolution 63/250, in which the duration of temporary appointments is limited to 729 days. The policy guidance issued in April 2020, by which heads of entities are granted certain exceptional authorities, including to extend the temporary appointments of currently serving staff members beyond 729 days, aimed at providing legal and administrative protection to the individuals concerned and the Organization, as a temporary measure applicable only during the COVID-19 pandemic period. The guidance clearly indicates that exceptional extension of appointments and contracts under these measures shall be strictly related to the COVID-19 context, for the absolute minimum period necessary and until the circumstances necessitating their use have abated (i.e. until travel restrictions have been lifted and travel out of the duty station is possible). The exceptional authorities expired on 31 July 2020.

history.recommendation_text: 17. The Board recommends that the Administration ensure that temporary appointments do not exceed 729 days.
history.reference_raw: A/75/5 (Vol. II), chap. II, for the period ended; para. 209
history.administration_response: The Administration stated it had provided sustained guidance and training to missions. This included the sharing of exceptions analysis and the issuance of the human resources exceptions guide in March 2021. This would enable entities to make rectifications in a timely manner and would ensure that exceptions not reported by missions could be captured in the exception log as soon as possible. In the two first quarters of 2021, no temporary appointment exceeding 729 days were detected in this regular monitoring, with the exception of one case at UNAMID. The Administration provided further statements by UNSOS, UNTSO, MONUSCO and UNFICYP regarding the various stages of implementation in those missions.
history.board_assessment: The Board stresses that the Staff Regulations and Rules prohibit that any temporary appointment exceed 729 days. While the Administration has demonstrated efforts to monitor temporary appointments exceeding 729 days and to reduce their number, these cases still exist. The Board considers this recommendation as under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration ensure that temporary appointments do not exceed 729 days.
history.administration_response: The Administration stated that as acknowledged by the Board in its latest comments, the Business Transformation and Accountability Division has put in place a comprehensive monitoring to capture all cases of temporary appointments extended beyond 729 days. The Division also liaises with entities when such cases are identified and requests them to take corrective actions when the extension beyond 729 days is the result of a calculation mistakes and requests them to report all other cases to the Assistant Secretary- General of the Office of Human Resources. The Division has also enhanced the human resources exceptions log to allow the Office of Human Resources to record all cases reviewed/taken note of/approved by the Assistant Secretary-General. As such, the Division considers this recommendation to be implemented. For information, no new case was detected during the second quarter of 2022. During the first quarter of 2022, three cases completed their appointments which had previously been extended beyond 729 days (two for UNAMID that ended on 31 Jan 2022, and one for MONUSCO that ended on 24 Feb 2022, 21 days beyond the authorized maximum).
history.board_assessment: The Board considers this recommendation as implemented, as the Administration has taken measures to implement monitoring measures.
